_note: Earned reforms, sandbox stops 4 and 5 of the open grand campaign only (the design director's one rule, 20 November 2026 05:33Z: a reform fires only from its own cause in that nation's war). Any nation may take them; none comes by date. The record's four dated events (red-army-1943, luftwaffe-1944, allied-armies-1944, german-army-1944) are not read there: these stand in their place. Causes, backstops and effects are the historian's (historian/sandbox-thresholds.md, end section, 05:38Z; tuned M). Counts: 'land' months with a land battle against a great power (the historian, 07:41Z, H: the 1939-40 Polish and Finnish fighting is already in the Soviet starting rating); 'trade' corps destroyed against corps lost (the memorial wall); 'factories' the share of its first-day factories it holds; 'peak' the most field corps it has had at once. Backstops count months in combat, never months at war. Stops 1 to 3 read none of this. DRAFT, not ruled in.

learns._who: A nation with slow command or a top attack below 14 (the Soviet Union and France at the start).

ofAge._who: An army rated below 1.0 that is not one that learns, and has not lost heart (heart.json: a junior partner's loss of heart overrides it). The record's America against Germany, Torch to Tunisia (39-45) and Sicily on: 12 land months at 51, 16 at 55 (the historian, 07:41Z, H). An army that never fights on land never comes of age.

ofAgeAir._who: Any nation: an enemy it is fighting has bled out ('bleeds'), after 'combat' months fighting that enemy (land battles or bombs either way); backstop: 'backstop' months bombing an enemy's home ground or being bombed on its own (the historian, 07:41Z: Britain, turn 9 to 57). The largest aircraft output among those at war with that enemy (air.json production) takes 'airMost', the rest 'air'. Who (the historian, 10:42Z, H): only a nation whose first-day air rating is below the best first-day air arm among the great powers, and never one that has bled. The record's coming of age was the others catching up with the Luftwaffe through training and numbers; the Luftwaffe never came of age again (its fighter pilots' training fell from about 250 hours to about 110 by 1944, against 400 or more for American pilots). Italy's case is fair if it has not bled (M: the C.202 of 1942).

bleeds._who: Any nation: 'raids' months of enemy day raids on its home ground by an enemy that holds 'tech'; backstop: 'backstop' months of enemy raids on its home ground, by day or by night, while an enemy holds 'backstopTech' (the historian, 07:41Z: British heavies from turn 18 give 54; by 1943-44 the night battle and the pull of fighters home wore the Luftwaffe down, M). The cause itself is day raids only.

cadre._who: An army rated 1.0 or more, once: the corps it has lost reach 'share' of its peak. No backstop. 0.6 is Germany's record losses against its peak at 55-58 (the historian, 07:41Z, H): Finland and Britain need no carve-out, since neither came near it in the record.

text.learns: The {adj} army has learned its trade in the hardest school. Its generals now handle whole armies in a single operation, and its air force has caught up with its enemies'.
text.ofAge: The {adj} army has come of age. Its divisions have learned their trade under fire, and behind every attack now stand guns, tanks and aircraft in numbers.
text.ofAgeAir: The {adj} air force has come into its own. Its squadrons have learned their trade and now hold the daylight sky over the battlefield.
text.bleeds: The {adj} air force has lost the daylight sky. Escorted bombers over its homeland have cost it pilots it cannot replace, and what is left is kept at home. The armies at the front will fight without it.
text.cadre: Years of losses have worn the {adj} army down. Its divisions are rebuilt with boys, older men and the half-recovered. They still fight with skill, but this is no longer the army that began the war.
